title.narrative: NIR - Ansvarsfull och hållbar gruvhantering i Latinamerika
NIR - Responsibility and sustainability in Latin American Mining

description.narrative:
NIR, along with the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) and Centro Vincular at the Pontificial Catholic University of Valparaíso (CV-PUCV) will work together in this contribution as a consortium. This contribution builds on the experience and networks of all its three core partner organisations and their complementary.
The programme has a regional scope, producing results at national and regional level, as well as locally in specific mining areas. It is also a programme that utilises the leverage of the Swedish and international mineral value chain and the Swedish resource base, including the Swedish mining cluster, embassies and trade promotion teams.
The Programme´s main objective is to contribute to "more responsible mining practices through inclusive processes with improved conditions for human rights and local environment". It will produce results on two different levels: two impact projects and a macro project, each project has a specific theory of change and is coordinated by one of the partner organizations:
1. Impact Project 1 called "Resource Management and Community Dialogue in Lithium Extraction" aims to establish regional commitments to a science-backed decision-making protocol that guarantees that lithium production remains within the sustainable capacity of salars in Argentina and Bolivia, following a previous successfully experience in Chile.
2. Impact Project 2 called "Multistakeholder Dialogue for Territorial Development in Mining Regions" has as its main objective to drive positive transformation for the local population in the mining provinces in Peru. To achieve this goal, they will implement an initiative that was already be proven effective by the IDB which focus on enhancing conditions for human rights, safeguarding the local environment, and fostering equitable development.
3. Impact project 4- in Colombia will focus on 3 components addressing key challenges in the mining sector. CO1: IMPLEMENTATION OF RESPONSIBLE MINING PRACTICES: Aim at implementing internationally recognized responsible business conduct (RBC) standards in the mining sector. CO2: WOMEN AND GENDERBASED CHALLENGES IN MINING: Aim at addressing challenges facing women in both largescale and small-scale mining. CO3: SUSTAINABILITY IN FORMAL SMALLSCALE MINING: Aim at improving environmental and human rights standards in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM). This Impact project has been added by a major amendment to the agreement signed on July 2024.
3. Macro Project aims at institutionalize results of the impact project at regional level by influencing decision makers in key stakeholder groups with regards to the implementation of responsible business conduct (RBC) and human rights standards in the mining sector. As part of the Macro Component, a Competence Centre (CC) will be developed and maintained to enable efficient knowledge management, consolidating information generated and lessons learned.
The main objective would be achieved through three main outcomes that will contribute to the impact of the project of protecting human rights, natural environment and a more equitable development through mining for the energy transition in LAC:
A. Companies in the mining value chain take responsibility for protecting human rights and contributing to local development, including through inclusive dialogue.
B. Public authorities implement their duty to protect human rights in connection with mining, including by enabling inclusive dialogue.
C. Mining affected populations and civil society organizations are empowered to protect the (human and collective) rights of mining affected populations, in particular through inclusive dialogue.

NIR, tillsammans med Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) och Centro Vincular vid katolska universitetet i Valparaíso (CV-PUCV) kommer att samarbeta i ett konsortium för genomförandet. Projektet bygger på erfarenhet, existerande nätverk och kompletterande kompetenser hos dessa tre partners.
Programmets huvudmål är att bidra till "mer ansvarsfull gruvdrift genom inkluderande processer som förbättrar förutsättningarna för att värna mänskliga rättigheter och lokal miljö". Resultat förväntas på två nivåer, genom två effektprojekt och ett makroprojekt. För varje projekt finns en förändringsteori och en av partnerorganisationerna ansvarar för koordineringen.
1. Effektprojekt 1: "Resurshantering och dialog med loklabefolkningen inom extraktion av lithium” syftar till att få till stånd regionala åtaganden för ett vetenskapligt underbyggt protokoll för beslutsfattande som garanterar att litiumproduktionen begränsas till ett hållbart uttag i saltöknarna i Argentina och Bolivia, i enlighet med en tidigare framgångsrik erfarenhet i Chile.
2. Effektprojekt 2: "Dialog med flera intressenter för territoriell utveckling i gruvregioner” har som huvudmål att driva positiva förändringar för lokalbefolkningen i gruvprovinserna i Peru. För att uppnå detta mål kommer att genomföras insatser, som i IDBs tidigare insatser visat sig effektiva, och som fokuserar på att förbättra villkoren för mänskliga rättigheter, skydda den lokala miljön och främja en rättvis utveckling.
3. Makroprojektet syftar till att institutionalisera resultaten av effektprojekten på regional nivå genom att påverka beslutsfattare i viktiga intressentgrupper för ansvarsfullt företagande och värnande av mänskliga rättigheter i gruvsektorn. Som en del av makroprojektet kommer ett kompetenscenter att inrättas för att möjliggöra effektiv kunskapshantering och konsolidering av genererad information och lärdomar.
Team Sweden-kategori: B: Sektor: Gruvindustri, land: Colombia

NIR, together with the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) and the Centro Vincular of the Catholic University of Valparaíso (CV-PUCV) will collaborate in a consortium for the implementation. The project is based on experience, existing networks and complementary competences of these three partners.
The program's main goal is to contribute to "more responsible mining through inclusive processes that improve the conditions for protecting human rights and the local environment". Results are expected on two levels, through two impact projects and a macro project. For each project there is a theory of change and one of the partner organizations is responsible for the coordination.
1. Impact project 1: "Resource management and dialogue with the local population in the extraction of lithium" aims to achieve regional commitments for a science-based decision-making protocol that guarantees that lithium production is limited to a sustainable extraction in the salt deserts of Argentina and Bolivia, in accordance with a previous successful experience in Chile.
2. Impact Project 2: "Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue for Territorial Development in Mining Regions" has as its main goal to drive positive changes for the local population in the mining provinces of Peru. To achieve this goal, efforts will be implemented, which in IDB's previous efforts have proven effective, and which focuses on improving conditions for human rights, protecting the local environment and promoting equitable development.
3. The macro project aims to institutionalize the results of the impact projects at the regional level by influencing decision-makers in important stakeholder groups for responsible business and the protection of human rights in the mining sector. As part of the macro project, a competence center will be established to enable effective knowledge management and consolidation of generated information and lessons learned.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement NIR MARS program - Sida Regional Latin America
Decision on Contribution 16558 - NIR MARS Program

description.narrative:
Main achievements in 2025 per project:
Impact Project 1 - Water Governance (Argentina)
Sida assesses that this project has made the most progress within the MARS Programme. In this project the objective is to create stronger conditions for inclusive water governance early in the mining cycle in the Salar de los Pastos Grandes.
1. Awareness and Commitment: Three agreements signed with the company Lithium Americas (now Lithium Argentina), the Secretariat of Mining and Energy of Salta Province and the Secretariat of Water Resources of Salta Province. The objective is to share key information to lay the groundwork for an inclusive, shared watershed modelling process in Salta.
2. Tools and Networks: MARS has secured inputs from date about specialised hydroclimatic information, gathered by Lithium Argentina with other sources in order to build a model, allowing watershed-scale analysis of water availability, ecosystem conditions, and existing pressures across the mining value chain.
The local community is participating in the co-developing the watershed tool, bringing together scientific inputs and Indigenous knowledge, while active participation in the process is strengthening its capacity to engage more confidently in future negotiations and decision-making for mutual benefit among the actors involved in Pastos Grandes.
A multidisciplinary Expert Council of Argentine academics, together with mining company and government data and local community knowledge, is bringing together complementary expertise to strengthen the models technical foundation over time.
This project has established partnerships with the Intergovernmental Forum on Mining, Minerals, Metals and Sustainable Development (IGF) to join efforts to build a Water Wise Lithium Development Protocol in Argentina. Moreover, with the Environmental Governance Programme (EGP) to identify potential synergies that could help define the terms of the final water management agreement relating to environmental monitoring and adaptive management.
Impact Project 2 - Territorial Dialogue and Development (Peru)
In this project, NIR seeks to provide actors with the tools, capacities and safe spaces for dialogue and solution co-development that can be embedded into existing institutional frameworks, and generate economic, social, and environmental value for all prioritised actors.
1. Awareness and Commitment: Territorial actors in Chumbivilcas and Pasco are participating in a more informed dialogue processes by adapting lessons from Cajamarca and Moquegua to their local contexts and by fostering alignment around shared development priorities, including environmental protection, womens participation, remediation, and education.
2. Tools and Networks: Early multi-stakeholder dialogue and coordination in Chumbivilcas and Pasco are being strengthened through the activation of key institutional networks: in Chumbivilcas, through MINEM, the Provincial Municipality, the Roundtable Against Poverty, and Hudbay; and in Pasco, through Regional Government leadership channelled via the Regional Environmental Commission and the Roundtable Against Poverty.
The lessons learned from previous experiences with IDB are being considered in this IP and NIR is working together with IDB.
Impact Project 3 - Colombia
This component is divided into two areas: 1) small-scale gold mining and 2) copper mining.
1. Small-scale gold mining
Awareness and commitment: The NIR has built a network of over 40 stakeholders and shifted the conversation from perceptions to practical discussions by gradually aligning around key barriers and emerging pathways. These include formalization, responsible supply chains, CRAFT standards, due diligence and traceability. The Embassy is aware of the important work carried out by the Alliance for Responsible Mining partner organization. However, we insist on seeing evidence of this work, which can be achieved by strengthening the monitoring and evaluation methodologies.
Tools and Networks: The baseline study of formal small-scale gold mining has been published and presented at events, territorial exchanges, webinars and as part of the Supply Chain Risk Management Diploma and Women in Mining training program. Together, these spaces have contributed to a stronger shared understanding and growing trust, as well as raising awareness of the barriers and opportunities affecting womens participation in the sector. In particular, the partnership with Women in Mining Colombia has created a dedicated platform to empower women, enhance their visibility, and boost their engagement. Around 450 people joined the webinars, 11 professionals completed the diploma and 18 women finished the training program.
As the Embassy participated in many of these events, we are familiar with the activities. We recommended to NIR that they measure changes in participants' perceptions and include some stories of change after the events.
2) copper mining
Progress on this component has been slower. They began the baseline study in collaboration with SEI in 2025, but it will not be published until 2026.
Awareness and commitment: a closed dialogue with the National Mining Agency, which provided input for the copper bidding rounds and related public documents, was a positive achievement.
Tools and Networks: Comments on governance, sustainability, and responsible mining standards were provided to the ANM for the copper bidding rounds, and were considered when defining the ToR for their design and development.
We expect to see further progress with this component by 2026.
Macro Project
The Macro Component operates at the national and regional levels, focusing on representatives from the business sector and communities to promote the consistent implementation of existing Responsible Business Conduct (RBC) frameworks.
1. Awareness and Commitment: Senior leadership engagement played a key role in mobilising associations as champions of the RBC agenda and elevating it within their strategic priorities. Member companies also deepened their involvement through two sessions on due diligence and stakeholder engagement, reaching 25 representatives. Regional alignment was strengthened through peerexchange sessions that highlighted good practices and strong leadership from Chiles Consejo Minero and Colombias ACM. These exchanges fostered early ownership for continuity, with all participating associations valuing the process and expressing interest in continuing in 2026.
2. Tools and Networks: Centro Vincular within the MARS programme developed an OECDendorsed selfassessment tool aligned with international frameworks, enabling mining associations to establish a shared baseline and define practical next steps to advance Responsible Business Conduct.
In 2025, an exploratory study was conducted, based on interviews with regional experts, designed to capture strategic perspectives from specialists with experience in Indigenous rights, territorial governance, socio-environmental conflict resolution, and relationships between communities and extractive projects. Several conclusions emerged that will guide the development of a Regional Protocol for Engagement between Indigenous Peoples and the mining sector.
As part of the macro project, a MARS Competence Centre is being developed in response to needs across the mining sector in Latin America: growing interest in learning settings, continued capacity strengthening, and stronger systems to retain and build on knowledge over time. The Centre is being designed as more than a digital platform, is envisioned as a practical and trusted platform for responsible and sustainable mining across the mining cycle. Rather than functioning as a static repository, it is intended to help users understand risks and access useful knowledge in clear and relevant ways.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
